source.title: FUN-SIS: a Fully UNsupervised approach for Surgical Instrument Segmentation
source.authors: Luca Sestini; Benoît Rosa; E. de Momi; G. Ferrigno; Nicolas Padoy

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses prior findings about memorization in deep networks and reports its own experiments on noisy segmentation masks. Those experiments do not test the listed claims about random image labels, training time, unstructured inputs, test error, regularization, or learning order.
record.gate_note: The study cites Arpit et al. (2017) for prior findings. Its own controlled-noise experiments replace segmentation masks with systematically eroded, randomly eroded or dilated, or dropped-tool masks; they do not use completely random image labels. Other reported segmentation scores are outside the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: Sections 3.2–3.4 use Arpit et al.'s shared-pattern-first finding to motivate Proxy training. The study reports segmentation quality and responses to structured mask corruption, but does not measure learning order, memorization of random labels, or the other specified effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the controlled-noise findings. The broader conclusion is that FUN-SIS trains surgical instrument segmentation from unlabelled videos using motion information and shape priors, approaching fully supervised performance in the tested datasets. The authors attribute the noisy-label strategy's effectiveness to unpredictability and polarization; they do not demonstrate the temporal learning-order claim.
record.recipe_differences: Experiments train segmentation networks on structured corruptions of segmentation masks, rather than random labels assigned to images.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise properties and corruption type (systematic erosion, erosion and dilation, or tool drop) change Proxy and Student outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: The Proxy fits predictable systematic erosion; with unpredictable erosion/dilation and tool omission, predictions improve over corrupted labels by averages of 13.76 and 29.75 IoU percentage points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The predictability of structured segmentation-label corruption affects whether a trained network reproduces that corruption or produces cleaner predictions.

fits_no_version.finding: Local region selection benefits Student training under polarized tool-omission noise, including 81.49% IoU at D20 and 88.98% and 88.41% at D80 and D60.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Region selection based on Proxy–label agreement can improve segmentation under polarized annotation noise.

record.code_released: The code will be released upon publication.
record.problems: The noise experiments use artificially corrupted segmentation masks, not random image labels. The relevant comparisons are presented in figures; the text reports selected averages and outcomes but not a full numerical breakdown for every corruption level.
record.rows_left_out: Other experiments report segmentation performance, shape-prior ablations, architecture comparisons, and optical-flow results. They do not address the listed claim versions and were not extracted.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and comparison using unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative time required to fit true and random labels, and convergence slowdown with increasing random-label corruption.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout a random-label corruption sweep and steadily worsening test error toward chance. Mask IoU levels are not fractions of randomly reassigned labels.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it impairs true-label generalization.
Temporal measurements showing shared real-data patterns learned before noisy labels. Final segmentation quality and architecture ablations do not establish this ordering.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's discusses/T6 classification to uses_without_test/T4: the memorization literature explicitly motivates the method. Structured segmentation corruption alone is not grounds for exclusion, but the reported measures do not establish any specified version. The cannot_determine states concern applicability to those versions, not whether the segmentation results occurred.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random image labels, training error, test error at chance, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence as the fraction of corrupted image labels changes.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Randomly corrupted image labels, perfect training fit across corruption fractions, and the relationship between test error and corruption fraction.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent fitting random image labels or are necessary for true-label generalization.
Whether networks learn real-label patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels over training.

rows.subject: Proxy network (Unet11)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on EndoVis2017VOS segmentation labels corrupted by systematic erosion; paper states the Proxy can fit this predictable noise.
rows.value: The Proxy network can perfectly learn to fit it, even when the corruption is minimal (D80).
rows.note: The result concerns structured segmentation-mask corruption, not random image labels.
rows.check: The authors explicitly describe fitting predictable systematic erosion, but this is structured corruption rather than completely random labeling. Figure 16 reports segmentation IoU against clean ground truth, not a direct measurement of zero training error.

rows.subject: Proxy network (Unet11)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on EndoVis2017VOS masks corrupted by random erosion or dilation; evaluated against ground-truth masks.
rows.measure: Mean IoU improvement over the noisy labels used for training
rows.note: This is a segmentation-mask experiment; the paper does not report training error or random image-label results.
rows.check: The reported 13.76 percentage-point IoU improvement measures segmentation quality relative to corrupted masks. It does not measure random-label training fit or the temporal order of learning signal and noise.

rows.subject: Proxy network (Unet11)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on EndoVis2017VOS masks with randomly dropped whole-tool annotations; evaluated against ground-truth masks.
rows.measure: Mean IoU improvement over the noisy labels used for training
rows.note: This is a segmentation-mask experiment; the paper does not report training error or random image-label results.
rows.check: The reported 29.75 percentage-point IoU improvement concerns randomly omitted tool annotations, which retain substantial input-related structure. It does not establish any listed version.

rows.subject: Student network (Unet16)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Tool-Drop-corrupted EndoVis2017VOS masks using local-IoU region selection.

conditions.value: D20 (∼20% IoU between training labels and GT)

rows.measure: Mean IoU on the evaluation set
rows.baseline: 88.99% reached by fully-supervised training of the Student model on clean labels
rows.note: The reported value is a segmentation evaluation result, not training error or test error under random image labels.
rows.check: This is performance of the study's region-selection method against a fully supervised baseline, not a claim-effect row. The 81.49% IoU result does not measure memorization or learning order.

rows.subject: Student network (Unet16)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Tool-Drop-corrupted EndoVis2017VOS masks using local-IoU region selection.
rows.measure: Mean IoU on the evaluation set
rows.note: These results concern corrupted segmentation masks, not random image labels.
rows.check: These are segmentation performance results for the study's region-selection method. Neither 88.98% nor 88.41% evaluation IoU establishes perfect training fit, random-label fitting, or signal-before-noise learning.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
